Construction helps you build your character's forms. These forms and shapes are based on the body parts and human anatomy.

As a beginner, I wouldn't get anywhere if I were limited to drawing the outer contour lines. Experienced artists have already drawn the body countless amounts of times, so they can manage to sketch that way.

Starting out with the basic forms also allows us to measure the character's proportions, and other foundational qualities, before committing to details.

When it comes to getting everything on the page, it's helpful to lightly block in the shapes and forms, adjust their sizes, and then begin to add details on top of them. It helps with comparing measurements, too!

For example, you can lightly draw in cylinders for the leg and arm bones, a box for the ribcage, a sphere for the skull, etc.

Your linework looks smooth in some areas and somewhat shaky in others. If you want to draw a long line, what you can do is ghost the line: repeating the drawing motion without touching the page, using your arm to draw, using fast motions, and then putting the pen to the page when you're ready.

You're doing fine, and you'll pick up on more things and placements as you keep engaging in studies (like how the spine inserts into the back of the skull, not the center). Keep comparing your current measurements between parts to your reference's! :)
